trace.code: type AuthOIDCServerConfig struct { Issuer string ...; Audience string `json:"audience,omitempty"` }  // empty => audience (client ID) verification is skipped
NewTokenVerifier builds oidc.Config{ClientID: cfg.Audience, SkipClientIDCheck: cfg.Audience == "", ...}
VerifyLogin calls verifier.Verify(...) then records token.Subject (no subject allowlist)

preconditions: frp server (frps) configured with OIDC authentication (auth.method = oidc) — opt-in, default is token auth
OIDC `audience` left unset (the field is optional/empty by default; the frp README example does set it)
attacker can obtain any valid ID token from the configured issuer — realistic for self-service/multi-tenant IdPs (Auth0-class) using the client-credentials grant

evidence.observed_result: With Audience unset (frp default) the verifier ACCEPTS an ID token minted for attacker-other-app (authentication bypass). With Audience set to legit-frp-client the same token is REJECTED (audience mismatch). Honest impact: a fail-open default that violates OIDC Core 3.1.3.7; realistic exploitation needs a self-service/multi-tenant IdP (client-credentials grant).
